ordering: Current release first; future order is indicative, not a dependency chain. Shared household timetable is explicitly last.

epics.title: Epic: Architecture and technical design
epics.goal: Keep system architecture and technical decisions in one place.

epics.title: Epic: Offline shopping
epics.goal: Use the shopping list reliably without a connection.

epics.title: Epic: Accounts and households
epics.goal: Sign in, share a household and manage who has access.

epics.title: Epic: Sync and collaboration
epics.goal: Keep household devices in agreement and make conflicts understandable.

epics.title: Epic: Products and shopping lists
epics.goal: Reuse products, support useful units and manage everyday shopping lists.

epics.title: Epic: Privacy, testing and release
epics.goal: Protect household data, verify the complete app and prepare a safe release.

epics.title: Future epic: Device-to-device sync
epics.goal: Let two authorized household devices exchange shopping changes nearby without internet.
discovery: Research supported iOS and Android discovery and transfer options.
Design explicit pairing and access checks, using the same shopping-change rules as cloud sync.
Test later cloud reconciliation; do not depend on NameDrop, touching phones or UWB.

discovery: Choose the first supermarkets and countries with the user.
Check available APIs, permission to use data and ongoing costs.
Design product matching, offer freshness and optional price comparison; ordering and retailer-account access need separate decisions.

epics.title: Future epic: Barcode scanning
epics.goal: Make it easier to find or add a product by scanning its barcode.
discovery: Choose a permitted product-data source and define what happens when a barcode is unknown.
Reuse the household catalog instead of creating duplicates.
Design the camera flow and offline fallback before implementation.

Preview additions to the shopping list so existing demand is not silently overwritten.
